title: Radó's theorem for Riemann surfaces
abstract: Proves that every connected Hausdorff one-dimensional complex manifold is second countable. The development constructs a nonconstant harmonic function by Perron's method, builds the étale space of its harmonic-conjugate germs, and applies a formalized Poincaré-Volterra lemma to its discrete-fiber evaluation map.

informal.rado_riemannSurface: Every connected Hausdorff topological space carrying the structure of a one-dimensional complex manifold has a second-countable topology.
informal.Rado.poincare_volterra: A connected Hausdorff, locally compact, locally connected and locally second-countable space is second countable whenever it admits a continuous, locally injective map into a second-countable Hausdorff space.
informal.Rado.exists_harmonic_extension: Every continuous real-valued function on a Euclidean circle extends continuously to its closed disk and harmonically to the open disk; unlike the existing LeanComplexAnalysis Poisson theorems, this constructs the harmonic function rather than assuming one.
informal.Rado.IsPerronFamily.surfaceHarmonicOn_pe: The pointwise upper envelope of a Perron family of surface subharmonic functions is harmonic on its open domain.
